module purpose: neorv32_cache is a direct-mapped cache between a host bus port (host_req_i/host_rsp_o) and a downstream bus port (bus_req_o/bus_rsp_i): its state machine (ctrl) buffers host requests and fences, sends uncached-region (address at or above UC_BEGIN), atomic and debug accesses straight downstream, serves read hits and writes through write hits using the neorv32_cache_memory instance (per-block valid bits, tags and byte-wide data arrays), downloads whole blocks on read misses, and invalidates a block whose download saw a bus error.

use-case flows.value: host access request: a host strobe, or a strobe held in ctrl.buf_req while the controller is busy, starts a lookup from S_IDLE
cache-bypass decision and direct access: uncached-region, atomic and debug accesses are sent downstream and the downstream response is returned to the host
lookup: tag and index of the request captured, valid bit and tag of the indexed block read, hit decided
cached data word of the indexed block returned to the host and acknowledged on a read hit
write hit: host byte enables write the cached word and the write is forwarded downstream (write-through); a write miss is forwarded without allocation

block download on a read miss: block address held in ctrl.tag, ctrl.idx and ctrl.ofs, each word requested downstream and written into the data array, block marked valid with its tag, word offset counted to the end of the block, then the lookup is repeated
download error: a downstream error during the block download is accumulated, the block is invalidated and the host receives an acknowledge with error
fence: a host fence (held in ctrl.buf_sync) clears every valid bit and is forwarded downstream when READ_ONLY = false
rstn_i low: controller forced to S_IDLE, request/fence/error/direct flags and block address cleared, all valid bits and the valid read register cleared

conceptual assets.concept: Cache controller state -- which phase of an access the cache is in (idle, lookup, direct response, clear, block download request/response/done)
conceptual assets.reasoning: Every flow is sequenced by `case ctrl.state is` (line 164): ctrl.state SELECTS the downstream strobe, address, lock and fence (lines 187-240), the cache commands cmd_clr, cmd_new and cmd_inv (lines 219, 226, 255), the host acknowledge and error (lines 191, 256-257) and the next state (lines 169-265). Integrity is Established: each of these outputs is defined only for its phase, so a corrupted state drives cache commands, downstream requests or host acknowledges outside the phase the flow defines. Availability is also Established under the implemented conditions: each state has an exit arm (lines 192, 211, 221, 231, 246-248, 258-260), unknown values return to S_IDLE (line 265) and rstn_i forces S_IDLE (line 117). ctrl.state stores it: `ctrl <= ctrl_nxt;` (line 126) registers the whole record on rising_edge(clk_i) (line 125), but the map puts CLOCKED_BY only on the whole record ctrl (occurrence 10) and gives the fields no CLOCKED_BY or COPIES record (MAP CHECK lists their RESET_BY as receiving without driving), so the reset assignment in the same clocked process (occurrence 2, line 117) is cited with a null edge. ctrl_nxt.state has COPIES ctrl.state (line 136) and drives only the register through line 126: it holds the next value, so the register is kept and ctrl_nxt.state is not listed.

conceptual assets.concept: Cache-bypass (direct access) decision -- whether the current host access goes straight to the downstream bus instead of through the cache
conceptual assets.reasoning: In S_IDLE `ctrl_nxt.buf_dir <= '1';` (line 173) is decided when the request address is at or above UC_BEGIN, or the access is atomic or debug (lines 171-172); in S_LOOKUP `if (ctrl.buf_dir = '1') then` (line 186) raises the downstream strobe and moves to S_DIRECT_RSP (lines 187-188), where the downstream response is returned (line 209). Integrity is Established: a wrong decision serves an uncached-region, atomic or debug access from the data array (lines 189-191), writes it into the cache (line 194) or allocates it by a block download (line 200), or bypasses the cache for a cacheable access. The values that decide it are fields of host_req_i, a transport port, so no setting input is reported. ctrl.buf_dir stores the decision and uses it (GATES bus_req_o.stb, cache_o.we, host_rsp_o.ack and ctrl_nxt.state at occurrence 3, line 186); the map misses the field-level clocked store at line 126 (whole-record assignment), so the reset occurrence (occurrence 2, line 121) is cited with a null edge. ctrl_nxt.buf_dir computes the next value and drives nothing but the register (line 126), so the register is kept and ctrl_nxt.buf_dir is not listed.

conceptual assets.concept: Pending host access request -- a host strobe remembered until the controller starts the lookup for it
conceptual assets.reasoning: `ctrl_nxt.buf_req <= ctrl.buf_req or host_req_i.stb;` (line 137) holds a strobe that arrives while the controller is not idle; in S_IDLE `elsif (host_req_i.stb = '1') or (ctrl.buf_req = '1') then` (line 170) starts the lookup (line 175), and S_LOOKUP clears the flag (line 184). Integrity is Established: a set flag starts a lookup and, through lines 187, 195 and 202, a downstream strobe for an access the host did not issue. Availability is also Established: for a one-cycle strobe outside S_IDLE the flag is the only record of the request, and it is held until the lookup consumes it. ctrl.buf_req stores it (GATES ctrl_nxt.state at occurrence 4, line 170); the map misses the field-level clocked store at line 126, so the reset occurrence (occurrence 2, line 118) is cited with a null edge. ctrl_nxt.buf_req holds the next value (drives only the register through line 126) and is not listed.

conceptual assets.concept: Pending fence request -- a host fence remembered until the cache is cleared
conceptual assets.reasoning: `ctrl_nxt.buf_sync <= ctrl.buf_sync or host_req_i.fence;` (line 138) holds a fence; in S_IDLE it has priority over requests (line 168) and moves to S_CLEAR (line 169), which asserts cache_o.cmd_clr (line 219, clearing every valid bit at line 381), forwards the fence downstream when READ_ONLY = false (lines 216-217) and clears the flag (line 220). Integrity is Established: if the flag is lost the valid bits stay set after the fence, so blocks the fence should discard keep producing hits (line 405) and returning their data (line 156); if it is spurious the cache is cleared and a fence is sent downstream without a host fence. Availability is also Established: the fence is held until S_CLEAR executes it. ctrl.buf_sync stores it (GATES ctrl_nxt.state at occurrence 4, line 168); the map misses the field-level clocked store at line 126, so the reset occurrence (occurrence 2, line 119) is cited with a null edge. ctrl_nxt.buf_sync holds the next value and is not listed.

conceptual assets.concept: Block download address -- tag, index and word offset of the block being fetched on a read miss
conceptual assets.reasoning: In S_LOOKUP the tag and index of the request address are captured (lines 180-181) and the word offset is zeroed (line 182). During the download the same value addresses both the downstream read (bus_req_o.addr, lines 227 and 238) and the cache-memory location and tag being written (cache_o.addr, lines 225 and 235, wired to addr_i at line 288; acc_tag, acc_idx, acc_off at lines 366-369; tag write at line 398, data write at lines 413-423). ctrl.ofs is incremented on each downstream acknowledge (line 244) and ends the download when all ones (lines 245-246). Integrity is Established: the word fetched downstream and the location and tag it is installed under must be the same address; a corrupted tag or index installs one address's data under another address's tag, which later read hits return (lines 191, 156), and a corrupted offset misplaces words or ends the download early. Availability is also Established under the implemented condition: the offset reaches all ones only through downstream acknowledges (line 243). ctrl.tag, ctrl.idx and ctrl.ofs store it (each SOURCES bus_req_o.addr, an output field, at lines 227 and 238; ctrl.ofs also GATES ctrl_nxt.state at line 245); the map misses their field-level clocked store at line 126, so the reset occurrences (lines 122-124) are cited with null edges. cache_o.addr only combines them toward the sub-unit (line 288) and is a carrier; ctrl_nxt.tag, ctrl_nxt.idx and ctrl_nxt.ofs hold the next values (COPIES at lines 141-143) and are not listed.

conceptual assets.concept: Download bus-error flag -- whether any downstream response during the current block download reported an error
conceptual assets.reasoning: `ctrl_nxt.buf_err <= ctrl.buf_err or bus_rsp_i.err;` (line 242) accumulates downstream errors during the download and S_LOOKUP clears the flag (line 183). In S_DOWNLOAD_DONE `if (ctrl.buf_err = '1') then` (line 254) asserts cache_o.cmd_inv (line 255) and returns an acknowledge with error (lines 256-257); otherwise the lookup is repeated (line 260). Integrity is Established: the block was marked valid when the download began (cmd_new at line 226, valid bit set at line 385), so a lost flag leaves a block holding errored data valid and the host gets no error, while a spurious flag invalidates a good block and reports an error. ctrl.buf_err stores it (GATES cache_o.cmd_inv, host_rsp_o.ack and host_rsp_o.err at occurrence 5, line 254); the map misses the field-level clocked store at line 126, so the reset occurrence (occurrence 2, line 120) is cited with a null edge. ctrl_nxt.buf_err holds the next value (COPIES ctrl.buf_err at line 139) and is not listed; host_rsp_o is a transport port.

conceptual assets.concept: Block validity state -- which cache blocks hold valid data, and the commands that set and clear it
conceptual assets.reasoning: neorv32_cache_memory keeps one valid bit per block: cleared by reset (line 377) and by clr_i (line 381), cleared for the indexed block by inv_i (line 383), set by new_i (line 385), and read for the indexed block into valid_mem_rd (line 387), which gates `hit_o <= '1' when (valid_mem_rd = '1') and (tag_mem_rd = acc_tag) else '0';` (line 405). Integrity is Established: a block may produce a hit only after a download installed it, and must stop after an error invalidation or a fence clear. The commands are decided in neorv32_cache: cache_o.cmd_new in S_DOWNLOAD_REQ (line 226), cache_o.cmd_inv in S_DOWNLOAD_DONE when ctrl.buf_err = '1' (line 255) and cache_o.cmd_clr in S_CLEAR (line 219); each is computed here from a decision (SELECTED_BY ctrl.state or GATED_BY ctrl.buf_err), so the sub-unit wiring exception holds, and each is wired to the memory (lines 283-285). In the memory, clr_i, inv_i and new_i set the state through their GATES records on valid_mem (lines 380-385). valid_mem_rd stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at line 387; GATES hit_o at line 405). valid_mem itself has only one use record, SOURCES valid_mem_rd (line 387), an internal register, so under the storing rule it is secondary and valid_mem_rd is the reference.

conceptual assets.concept: Block tag directory -- the address tag recorded for each cache block and compared on lookup
conceptual assets.reasoning: When new_i is set the tag of the accessed address is written into the indexed entry, `tag_mem(to_integer(unsigned(acc_idx))) <= acc_tag;` (line 398); the indexed entry is read into tag_mem_rd (line 400), and a hit requires `tag_mem_rd = acc_tag` (line 405). acc_tag is a slice of addr_i (line 366). Integrity is Established: the stored tag must identify the address whose words occupy the block; a wrong tag produces hits that return another address's data (lines 191, 156). addr_i sets it, since this entity reads it to form the tag it stores and compares (SOURCES acc_tag at line 366; it also forms the index and offset at lines 367-368); new_i sets it (GATES tag_mem at line 397); tag_mem_rd stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at line 400; CONSTRAINS hit_o at line 405). tag_mem's only use record is SOURCES tag_mem_rd (line 400), an internal register, so it is secondary. acc_tag is a slice and an operand of the comparison, not its result.

conceptual assets.concept: Cache hit decision -- whether the indexed block is valid and holds the requested address
conceptual assets.reasoning: `hit_o <= '1' when (valid_mem_rd = '1') and (tag_mem_rd = acc_tag) else '0';` (line 405) is the comparison result. It reaches neorv32_cache on cache_i.sta_hit (line 286), where `elsif (cache_i.sta_hit = '1') then` (line 189) chooses between acknowledging a read from the cache (line 191), a write-through update of the data array (lines 194-196), and a block download or direct write on a miss (lines 199-203). Integrity is Established: a false hit acknowledges the data array contents of an invalid or different block (lines 191, 156); a false miss forwards a write without updating the cached copy or repeats a download. hit_o is the exit port of neorv32_cache_memory (CONSTRAINED_BY tag_mem_rd at line 405). cache_i.sta_hit is a record field that receives a sub-unit output; it is tested in the if at line 189, so the wiring exception holds, and it is where the decision enters neorv32_cache (CONNECTS from hit_o at line 286).

conceptual assets.concept: Cached block data -- the data words held in the cache and returned on read hits
conceptual assets.reasoning: data_mem_b0 to data_mem_b3 hold the cached bytes: written under we_i from wdata_i (lines 413-423) and read at acc_adr into rdata_o (lines 425-428), which reaches the host through cache_i.data (lines 291, 156) and is acknowledged on a read hit (line 191). The written word is the downloaded word (`cache_o.data <= bus_rsp_i.data;` line 236) or the host write data on a write hit (lines 151, 194). Integrity is Established: a read hit must return the word downloaded or last written for that address. Availability is also Established: the arrays hold their contents between writes and rdata_o is registered on every clock edge (line 412). wdata_i sets it (SOURCES data_mem_b0 at line 414); data_mem_b0 to data_mem_b3 store it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i; SOURCES rdata_o, an output port of their entity, at lines 425-428); rdata_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM data_mem_b0 at line 425), ahead of its own storage role. cache_o.data (COPIES host_req_i.data or bus_rsp_i.data, lines 151, 236) and cache_i.data (CARRIES host_rsp_o.data, line 156) only pass the word between the entities and are carriers; host_rsp_o, host_req_i and bus_rsp_i are transport. Confidentiality is not established: no line restricts which requester reads the array (host_req_i.priv has no local use).

conceptual assets.concept: Data-array write enable decision -- whether, and which bytes of, the cached word are written
conceptual assets.reasoning: cache_o.we is all zeros by default (line 150), the host byte enables on a write hit outside direct mode (`cache_o.we <= host_req_i.ben;` line 194, under lines 186, 189 and 190), and all ones while a downloaded word is installed (line 237); it is wired to we_i (line 289), which gates each byte array (lines 413-423). Integrity is Established: the data array may change only on a write hit, and then only in the enabled bytes, or during a block download; a spurious enable overwrites cached words that later read hits return (line 191), and a missing enable leaves the cached copy stale after the write-through of line 195. In builds with READ_ONLY = true the write-hit arm is unreachable (line 190), so only the download enable remains. cache_o.we computes the decision here (GATED_BY cache_i.sta_hit, ctrl.buf_dir and host_req_i.rw at occurrence 3, line 194), so the sub-unit wiring exception holds; we_i sets it in the memory (GATES data_mem_b0 at line 413, and the other byte arrays at lines 416-422).
